rows.speaker: الجمهور، ابن مقسم، الكسائي عن الحسن
rows.claim: The majority reads al-fulk in the accusative; Ibn Miqsam and al-Kisāʾī, reporting from al-Ḥasan, are cited for a lām-damma pronunciation.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور والفلك بالنصب وضم اللام ابن مقسم والكسائي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers coordinating the accusative ship noun with ما; singling it out despite its inclusion highlights the ships’ remarkable subjection and benefits.
rows.anchor: وانتصب عطفا على ما ونبه عليها وإن كانت

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative coordinates al-fulk with the divine name by supplying “and the ships”; Abū Ḥayyān calls this parsing inelegant.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون معطوفا على الجلالة بتقدير وأن الفلك

rows.speaker: السلمي والأعرج وطلحة وأبو حيوة والزعفراني
rows.claim: These readers pronounce kāf with ḍamma as a subject with a predicate; coordination at the syntactic position of إن makes تجري circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والأعرج وطلحة وأبو حيوة والزعفراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent parsing puts أن تقع in the accusative as a بدل اشتمال, meaning God prevents the sky from falling onto earth.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أن تقع في موضع نصب بدل اشتمال

rows.speaker: البصريون والكوفيون
rows.claim: The Basrans take the phrase as a causal object with an implied “for fear”; the Kufans understand an implied “lest it fall.”
rows.anchor: هو مفعول من أجله يقدره البصريون كراهة أن تقع والكوفيون لأن لا تقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception can evoke the sky’s folding on Judgment Day as part of its falling; it also attaches to falling, which occurs only by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: وقوله إلا بإذنه أي يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also be a warning that if God permitted the sky to fall in fragments on the deniers, it would fall, as they challenged.
rows.anchor: وعيدا لهم في أنه إن أذن في سقوطها كسفا عليكم سقطت

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches the exception to God’s holding the sky; Abū Ḥayyān objects that the intended sense would simply say “by His permission,” without an exception particle.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يعود قوله إلا بإذنه على الإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revived people after they were inert as dust, then sperm, clot, and lump; this is the first death and revival mentioned in 2:28.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي أحياكم أي بعد أن كنتم جمادا ترابا ونطفة وعلقة ومضغة وهي الموتة الأولى المذكورة في قوله تعالى كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies “the human” as the disbeliever; named individuals are illustrative examples.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafūr means one who repudiates and is ungrateful for God’s blessings, worshipping someone other than the benefactor who gave these and other blessings.
rows.anchor: لكفور لجحود لنعم الله، يعبد غير من أنعم عليه بهذه النعم المذكورة وبغيرها

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A reported occasion is a dispute about sacrificial meat: polytheists including Budayl ibn Warqāʾ and Bishr ibn Sufyān challenged Muslims for eating animals they slaughtered but not those God killed.
rows.anchor: روي أنها نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار بديل بن ورقاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says “they perform it” shows mansak is a verbal noun, since a place noun would require “in it”; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the necessity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية هم ناسكوه يعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle can take a locative complement directly by extension, just as a verb can; the place is treated like a direct object.
rows.anchor: ولا يتعين ما قال إذ قد يتسع في معمول اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited anonymous poem uses مشرب for a drinking place and attaches a pronoun directly; its underlying sense is “I drink in it.”
rows.anchor: ومشرب أشربه رسيل ... لا آجن الماء ولا وبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel over two farsakhs is another extension in a locative expression.
rows.anchor: ومن الاتساع سير بزيد فرسخان

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A reading with a light nūn tells the Prophet to remain firm in his religion so opponents cannot draw him into theirs.
rows.anchor: أي اثبت على دينك ثباتا لا يطمعون أن يجذبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is rhetorically directed at opponents, like “do not let me see you here,” though their dispute will try to provoke the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا النهي لهم عن المنازعة من باب لا أرينك

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Mujliz reads the verb from نزع, “to pull away,” meaning they must not uproot the Prophet from his religion and carry him to theirs.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز فلا ينازعنك من النزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amr means the religion and message brought by the Prophet; given the reported occasion, it can instead mean the slaughtering dispute.
rows.anchor: وعلى ما روي في سبب النزول يكون في الأمر بمعنى في الذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā here means guidance or right direction.
rows.anchor: هدى أي إرشاد. وجاء ولكل أمة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says 22:34 has a conjunction because it follows related verses about sacrificial rites, while this verse lacks one because its context is semantically distant.
rows.anchor: فلم تجد معطفا قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls this a verse of forbearance abrogated by the Sword Verse.
rows.anchor: وإن جادلوك آية موادعة نسختها آية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they persist in arguing after the Prophet’s effort to avoid dispute, he should answer that God knows their deeds and deserved recompense; the warning is gentle.
rows.anchor: أي وإن أبو للجاجهم إلا المجادلة بعد اجتهادك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses believers and unbelievers, promising to decide between them by reward and punishment; this consoles the Prophet for their treatment of him.
rows.anchor: الله يحكم بينكم خطاب من الله للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the separation of believers and unbelievers at resurrection, the passage stresses that God knows all things, so no deeds are hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الفصل بين الكفار والمؤمنين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the Book as the Mother of the Book, written before creation and containing everything that will occur until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو أم الكتاب الذي كتبه الله قبل خلق

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Book as the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكتاب اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative takes “that” as the prior divine judgment; Abū Ḥayyān’s apparent reading makes it refer to all creatures encompassed by God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل: إلى الحكم السابق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God knows all events and recorded them in the Tablet before they occurred; encompassing, recording, and preserving them are easy for the One who knows by His essence.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومعلوم عند العلماء بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān detects a Muʿtazilī implication in “knowing by His essence,” since the Muʿtazila deny divine attributes and say God knows by His essence.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله لأن العالم الذات فيه دسيسة الاعتزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols have no revealed, heavenly warrant or proof from revelation and transmitted authority.
rows.anchor: أي حجة وبرهانا سماويا من جهة الوحي والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also lack any knowledge-based proof, whether necessary rational evidence or another kind.
rows.anchor: أي دليل عقلي ضروري أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who exceed bounds by worshipping what cannot be worshipped; they have no helper to support their claim or rescue them at punishment.
rows.anchor: وما للظالمين أي المجاوزين الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger or another recites clear signs that refute the idols and call people to God’s oneness and worship.
rows.anchor: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا أي يتلوه الرسول أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers have covered up manifest truth; al-munkar is a verbal noun meaning rejection or disapproval.
rows.anchor: الذين ستروا الحق وغطوه وهو واضح بين والمنكر مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit mention of “those who disbelieved” replaces a pronoun to identify the cause of their visible disapproval.
rows.anchor: وناب الظاهر مناب المضمر كأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-munkar appears as displeasure, scowling, frowning, and aggression, exposing bad belief and inner corruption.
rows.anchor: والمنكر المساءة والتجهم والبسور والبطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face reveals the heart’s sadness and joy.
rows.anchor: لأن الوجه يظهر فيه الترح والفرح اللذان محلهما القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their near-attack is a lasting disposition, though they did assault some Companions on rare occasions.
rows.anchor: يكادون يسطون أي هم دهرهم بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains يسطون as reaching or stretching their hands toward the reciters.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يسطون يبسطون إليهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb explains يسطون as falling upon or attacking the reciters.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: يقعون بهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains يسطون as seizing the reciters with their hands; Abū Ḥayyān says the explanations amount to the same thing.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يأخذونهم أخذا باليد

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads يعرف in the passive, making al-munkar the subject recognized on their faces.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر يعرف مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat and rebuke point either to their rage and attacks against reciters or to the distress and scowling caused by the recitation.
rows.anchor: هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلكم وعيد وتقريع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads النار nominative, with an implied subject: if asked what is worse, the answer is the Fire of Hell.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور النار رفعا على إضمار مبتدأ

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows النار as subject with وعدها as predicate, or وعدها as a circumstantial clause under the implied-subject parsing, or a new declarative sentence.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن تكون النار مبتدأ

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another parsing treats the clause as a second predicate under the first nominative analysis.
rows.anchor: وأجيز أن تكون خبرا بعد خبر

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A report says the opponents called Muḥammad and his Companions the worst creatures; God’s reply identifies the disbelievers themselves as people of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم قالوا: محمد وأصحابه شر خلق

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وإبراهيم بن يوسف عن الأعشى وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: These readers read النار in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وإبراهيم بن يوسف عن الأعشى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses the accusative as specification and says one who permits the nominative subject should also allow an accusative اشتغال construction.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: على الاختصاص ومن أجاز في الرفع

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وإبراهيم بن نوح عن قتيبة
rows.claim: These readers read النار in the genitive as an appositive to شر.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وإبراهيم بن نوح عن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes Fire the first object promised: God has promised it to the disbelievers as their food.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في وعدها هو المفعول الأول

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another parsing makes Fire the second object and the disbelievers the first, as in the formulation that God promised them Hell.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير هو المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying idolaters lack any revealed or rational warrant and abandon their Creator, the text demonstrates that idols cannot create even a fly or recover what it takes.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى أن الكفار يعبدون ما لا دليل على عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address in “you invoke” is directed to polytheists who worship beings besides God.
rows.anchor: لقوله إن الذين تدعون بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes the address as aimed at believers, explaining the unbelievers’ error.
rows.anchor: خطاب للمؤمنين أراد الله أن يبين لهم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further view takes the address as general: anyone who reflects on worshipping other than God sees its ugliness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخطاب عام يشمل من نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضرب is passive; the apparent agent of the example is God, who presents the powerless idols as an analogy and tells people to consider it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ضارب المثل هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An alternative makes the polytheists the agents: they set their idols as peers of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضارب المثل هم الكفار

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says there is no explicit “example” here; the meaning is that the polytheists made a peer for God.
rows.anchor: ما قال الأخفش قال: ليس هاهنا مثل وإنما المعنى

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation says it is an example in meaning, comparing idol worshippers to people who worship something incapable of creating a fly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل من حيث المعنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that an appealing or astonishing story may be called a mathal by comparison with admired and surprising circulating proverbs.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: الذي جاء به ليس بمثل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads تدعون with tāʾ, active.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تدعون بالتاء

rows.speaker: الحسن ويعقوب وهارون والخفاف ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Yaʿqūb, Hārūn, al-Khaffāf, and Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr read with yāʾ, active.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ويعقوب وهارون والخفاف

rows.speaker: اليماني وموسى الأسواري
rows.claim: Al-Yamānī and Mūsā al-Aswārī read with yāʾ in the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليماني وموسى الأسواري بالياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says lan emphatically negates the future here to show that creating a fly is impossible for the idols.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري لن أخت لا في نفي المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī applies his claim that lan negates forever; grammarians correctly treat it like lā in negation.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول الذي قاله في لن هو المنقول عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān supports the ordinary parsing of lan by citing “Can one who creates be like one who does not create?” (16:17).
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument first denies the idols’ exclusive divine power to originate creation, then intensifies the challenge with their inability to retrieve what a fly takes.
rows.anchor: وبدأ تعالى بنفي اختراعهم وخلقهم أقل المخلوقات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Arabs smeared idols with saffron and honey, then shut them away; flies entered through openings and ate it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: كانوا يطلونها بالزعفران

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses ولو اجتمعوا له as circumstantial: creating a fly remains impossible even if all the idols gathered and cooperated.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān instead coordinates the clause with an implicit “in every state”: even gathering and cooperating cannot give them power to create.
rows.anchor: وتقرر أن الواو فيه للعطف على حال محذوفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the seeker as the idol and the sought as the fly: the idol should seek back its stolen perfume.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الصنم والذباب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view reverses the roles: idols are sought and weak because they cannot defend themselves; the fly is the seeker and weak in stealing from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل المطلوب الآلهة والطالب الذباب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the seeker as the worshipper and the sought as the worshipped: the worshipper seeks good from the wrong source, and the idol cannot provide it.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: العابد والمعبود

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the wording levels idol and fly in weakness, though the idol is weaker because it is inanimate while the fly is alive and victorious.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقوله ضعف الطالب والمطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is a statement that both seeker and sought are weak.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه إخبار بضعف الطالب والمطلوب

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the wording exclamatory: “How weak are the seeker and the sought!”
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه التعجب أي ما أضعف الطالب والمطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have not truly known or esteemed God: they worship beings stripped of His attributes and assign them His name, while failing to worship their Creator.
rows.anchor: ما قدروا الله حق قدره أي ما عرفوه حق معرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close emphasizes strength and might, attributes opposed to the weakness and impotence of the idols.
rows.anchor: ثم ختم بصفتين منافيتين لصفات آلهتهم

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: The reported occasion is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra’s objection that revelation came to Muḥammad rather than another notable; God answers that messengers are chosen from angels and humans.
rows.anchor: الآية نزلت بسبب قول الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the states of those morally responsible, nothing is hidden from Him, and all affairs return to Him.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر أنه عالم بأحوال المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing God’s choice of human messengers, the text orders believers to establish the obligations those messengers brought.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى أنه اصطفى رسلا من البشر

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A report says early Muslims initially prostrated without bowing or bowed without prostrating, so they were ordered to combine both in prayer.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان الناس أول ما أسلموا

rows.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد وعمر وابنه عبد الله وعثمان وأبو الدرداء وأبو موسى وابن عباس
rows.claim: All agree on prostration at 22:18; for this verse, Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfa do not prescribe prostration, while al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the listed Companions do.
rows.anchor: واتفقوا على مشروعية السجود في آخر آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship your Lord means to single Him out in worship.
rows.anchor: اعبدوا ربكم أي أفردوه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses doing good as maintaining family ties and practicing noble character.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صلة الأرحام ومكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands move from prayer, to the broader category of worship, then to the still wider category of good deeds.
rows.anchor: ويظهر في هذا الترتيب أنهم أمروا أولا بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihād for God includes striving in His religion and for His word, against unbelievers and innovators, and against the self.
rows.anchor: أمر بالجهاد في دين الله وإعزاز كلمته

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A narrower interpretation limits the command to fighting unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر بجهاد الكفار خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As is due” means to expend one’s full effort and capacity in the struggle.
rows.anchor: حق جهاده أي استفرغوا جهدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attachment to God is apt because the struggle is solely for His sake and on His account; a loose relation suffices for annexation.
rows.anchor: وأضاف الجهاد إليه تعالى لما كان مختصا بالله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows an extended prepositional phrase: the original would be حق جهاد فيه, with the preposition omitted and جهاد annexed to the pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يتسع في الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حق جهاده is an emphatic idiom meaning “truly” or “to the utmost,” like saying someone is truly learned.
rows.anchor: وحق جهاده من باب هو حق عالم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Kalbī say the command to strive fully was abrogated by “fear God as much as you are able.”
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد والكلبي أنه منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose the community to bear His obligations; the emphatic هو means He alone chose them.
rows.anchor: هو اجتباكم أي اختاركم لتحمل تكليفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion is free of constriction and is a lenient way without Israelite severity, including repentance, expiations, and legal concessions.
rows.anchor: من تضييق بل هي حنيفية سمحة ليس فيها تشديد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted verb, جعلها ملة, to govern the accusative ملة.
rows.anchor: وقدره ابن عطية جعلها ملة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects the accusative to the preceding sense: God widened the religion as Abraham’s way, with an omitted genitive head, or as specification.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: نصب الملة بمضمون ما تقدمها

rows.speaker: الحوفي وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ take the phrase as an imperative: follow Abraham’s way.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي وأبو البقاء: اتبعوا ملة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ posits an omitted kāf, effectively “like the way of your father,” and explains Abraham as the community’s father through the Messenger’s relation to him.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو نصب على تقدير حذف الكاف

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation attributes Abraham as father because most of the Messenger’s people and Arabs descend from him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما كان أكثرهم من ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Abraham concerns worshipping God and abandoning idols; it does not require following every detail of Abraham’s legal system.
rows.anchor: وجاء قوله ملة إبراهيم باعتبار عبادة الله وترك الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of هو is Abraham; Abraham prayed for a Muslim community from his descendants, and God answered by making it Muḥammad’s community.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في هو سماكم عائد على إبراهيم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and al-Ḥasan are cited for the view that Abraham named the community Muslims.
rows.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام، وقاله ابن زيد والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk instead take هو to refer to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعود هو إلى الله وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God called the community Muslims in earlier scriptures and now in the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن الله سماكم المسلمين من قبل

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading “God named you” supports taking هو as God.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن الضمير لله قراءة أبي الله سماكم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says “and in this” weakens the Abraham antecedent unless an omitted sentence is supplied.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذه اللفظة يعني قوله وفي هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān supplies “and you were named Muslims in this Qurʾān”; on that reading God favored the community and gave it this name.
rows.anchor: وتقدير المحذوف وسميتم في هذا القرآن المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger witnesses that he delivered the message, and the community witnesses that messengers delivered to their peoples; believers should worship, trust, and seek aid only from God.
rows.anchor: ليكون الرسول شهيدا عليكم أنه قد بلغكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says this community received privileges given only to a prophet, including the Prophet’s witness over his people, relief from hardship, and the assurance that if he asks he will be given.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أعطيت هذه الأمة ما لم يعطه إلا نبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Continuing Qatāda’s report, the community was appointed witness over humanity, relieved of hardship, and told to call on God for a response.
rows.anchor: لهذه الأمة: وتكونوا شهداء على الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains holding fast to God as asking Him to protect you from everything disliked.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس سلوا ربكم أن يعصمكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains holding fast to God as adhering to God’s religion.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن تمسكوا بدين الله

rows.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
rows.claim: A woman from the Anṣār complained that male relatives kept entering her home while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: جاءت امرأة من الأنصار إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: After the verse was revealed, Abū Bakr asked about inns and dwellings without residents, and the permission for entering uninhabited houses was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر بعد نزولها: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule follows the slander episode: seclusion gave slanderers an opening, so entering another person’s house requires permission and greeting to prevent suspicion and harm.
rows.anchor: هو أن أهل الإفك إنما وجدوا السبيل إلى بهتانهم من حيث اتفقت الخلوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes the wording to imply that a person may enter their own home without asking permission or greeting.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه يجوز للإنسان أن يدخل بيت نفسه

rows.speaker: رجل غير مسمى
rows.claim: A man asked whether he must seek permission before entering on his mother, though he was her only attendant; the Prophet asked whether he wanted to see her naked, and he said no.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of istīʾnās is relief from unease: a person knocking does not know whether entry will be permitted and becomes at ease after permission.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الاستئناس هو خلاف الاستيحاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording parallels the rule that one must not enter the Prophet’s houses except with permission; istīʾnās is a metonym and follow-on expression for permission.
rows.anchor: كقوله: لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to gloss تستأنسوا as “seek permission.”
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال تستأنسوا معناه تستأذنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān condemns as heretical the claim that Ibn ʿAbbās called تستأنسوا a copyist’s error and read تستأذنوا; he declares Ibn ʿAbbās innocent of it.
rows.anchor: ومن روي عن ابن عباس أن قوله تستأنسوا خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word تستأنسوا is sound and meaningful in Arabic according to its intended usage.
rows.anchor: وتستأنسوا متمكنة في المعنى بنية الوجه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: The report that ʿUmar asked “May I seek comfort, Messenger of God?” at the room’s door shows the word can mean seeking familiarity with him.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أستأنس يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the word from inquiry: ascertain whether entry is wanted, as in asking whether anyone is visible or saying one looked and saw nobody.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من الاستئناس الذي هو الاستعلام والاستكشاف

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s phrase “على مستأنس وحد” is cited for the sense of someone who can be seen or found alone.
rows.anchor: ومنه بيت النابعة: كأن رحلي وقد زال النهار بنا

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A further possibility derives the word from uns: check whether a human being is present.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الأنس وهو أن يتعرف

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب
rows.claim: Abū Ayyūb reports that the Prophet said istīʾnās is alerting a household by saying tasbīḥ or takbīr or clearing one’s throat; greeting means saying “peace be upon you.”
rows.anchor: وعن أبي أيوب قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a visitor might call out a morning or evening greeting and enter, potentially finding a man with his wife under one blanket; God prevented this and taught better etiquette.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يقول الرجل منهم إذا دخل بيتا غير بيته

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says visitors should alert the household by clearing the throat, asking permission, or similar means, and ensure the household noticed them.
rows.anchor: وذهب الطبري في تستأنسوا إلى أنه بمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues that the verb’s morphology prevents deriving it from آنس.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وتصريف الفعل يأبى

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says permission is obligatory for every adult; Abū Ḥayyān’s apparent ruling requires permission generally and considers one request sufficient.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: الاستئذان واجب على كل محتلم
